newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil refinances 50.4 bln reais in Sao Paulo debt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil refinances 50.4 bln reais in Sao Paulo debt.

text.p: The Brazilian government signed a deal Thursday to refinance 50.4 billion reais in debt held by Sao Paulo state, taking over for the time being the state bank Banespa, the Finance Ministry said.
In a statement, the Finance Ministry said the debt would be refinanced with a 30-year maturity and interest of 6.0 percent a year, adjusted for inflation.
The deal will be paid for by the issue of 37.5 billion reais in 15-year Treasury Financial Letters (LFTs) and 10.3 billion reais in LFTs with maturities of between one month and eight years.
Part of Sao Paulo state's debt will be retired through the sale of shares in Banespa, electricity distributor Eletropaulo and other state-run companies.

Privatizations must be completed by the end of November 1998 under the deal, and fiscal adjustments must be carried out to ensure Sao Paulo state's debt stock is gradually reduced to equal its net annual receipts by 2008.
Fifty-one percent of the voting stock of Banespa will be transferred to the federal government.
"The institution could be either privatized or returned to the state," the statement said.

Of the total debt assumed, 20.1 billion reais refers to Sao Paulo securities bought by Banespa, state mortgage bank Nossa Caixa and another bank, Nosso Banco; 24.4 billion reais refers to contractual debt owed by the state to Banespa and 5.9 billion to contractual debt owed to Nossa Caixa and Nosso Banco.
The debt restructuring deal was announced several months ago but was held up because of last minute difficulties and disagreements.
